translation_en: Khal lad narrated to us; Misar narrated to us, from Habib ibn Abi Thabit, from Abu al-Shathaa, from Hudhayfah, who said: Hypocrisy existed during the time of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him. As for today, it is disbelief after faith.

Ismail narrated to us: Malik narrated to me, from Abu al-Zinad, from al-Araj, from Abu Hurairah, from the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, who said: “The Hour will not come until a man passes by another man's grave and says: ‘Would that I were in his place.’”

Abu al-Yaman informed us; Shuayb informed us, from al-Zuhri, who said: Said ibn al-Musayyab said: Abu Hurairah, may Allah be pleased with him, informed me that the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: “The Hour will not come until the buttocks of the women of Daws sway around Dhu al-Khalasah.” Dhu al-Khalasah was the idol of Daws that they worshipped in the pre-Islamic age.

Abd al-Aziz ibn Abdullah narrated to us; Sulayman narrated to me, from Thawr, from Abu al-Ghayth, from Abu Hurairah, that the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: “The Hour will not come until a man from Qahtan emerges, driving the people with his staff.”

Abu al-Yaman informed us; Shuayb informed us, from al-Zuhri, who said: Said ibn al-Musayyab said: Abu Hurairah informed me that the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: “The Hour will not come until a fire emerges from the land of the Hijaz, illuminating the necks of camels at Busra.”

Abdullah ibn Said al-Kindi narrated to us; Uqbah ibn Khalid narrated to us; Ubaydullah narrated to us, from Khubayb ibn Abd al-Rahman, from his grandfather Hafs ibn Asim, from Abu Hurairah, who said: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: “The Euphrates is about to uncover a treasure of gold. Whoever is present there should take nothing from it.” Uqbah said: Ubaydullah also narrated to us, from Abu al-Zinad, from al-Araj, from Abu Hurairah, from the Prophet, a similar report, except that he said: “It will uncover a mountain of gold.”

Musaddad narrated to us; Yahya narrated to us, from Shu'bah. Mabid narrated to us: I heard Harithah ibn Wahb say: I heard the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, say: “Give charity, for a time will come upon people when a man will walk with his charity and find no one to accept it.” Musaddad said: Harithah was the maternal brother of Ubaydullah ibn Umar. Abu Abdullah said this.

Abu al-Yaman informed us; Shuayb informed us; Abu al-Zinad narrated to us, from Abd al-Rahman, from Abu Hurairah, that the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: “The Hour will not come until two great groups fight, and there will be a great slaughter between them, though their claim is one; until lying impostors, nearly thirty of them, are sent forth, each claiming to be a Messenger of Allah; until knowledge is taken away, earthquakes increase, time draws closer, trials appear, and killing becomes widespread; and until wealth among you becomes abundant and overflows, so that the owner of wealth will worry about who will accept his charity, and will offer it to someone who says: ‘I have no need of it.’ The Hour will not come until people compete in building tall structures; until a man passes another man's grave and says: ‘Would that I were in his place’; and until the sun rises from the west. When it rises and people see it, they will all believe, but then faith will not benefit a soul that did not believe before or earn good through its faith. The Hour will come while two men have spread a garment between them but will neither complete the sale nor fold it away; while a man has returned with the milk of his she-camel but will not drink it; while a man is plastering his water basin but will not use it to water anything; and while a man has raised a bite of food to his mouth but will not eat it.”

Musaddad narrated to us; Yahya narrated to us; Ismail narrated to us; Qays narrated to me, who said: al-Mughirah ibn Shubah said to me: “No one asked the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, about the Dajjal as much as I did. He said to me: ‘What harm could he do you?’ I said: ‘They say he will have a mountain of bread and a river of water.’ He said: ‘He is of less consequence to Allah than that.’”

Musa ibn Ismail narrated to us; Wuhayb narrated to us; Ayyub narrated to us, from Nafi, from Ibn Umar—I think he reported it from the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him—who said: “He is blind in his right eye, like a floating grape.”

Sad ibn Hafs narrated to us; Shayban narrated to us, from Yahya, from Ishaq ibn Abdullah ibn Abi Talhah, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: “The Dajjal will come and stop at the outskirts of Medina. Then Medina will be shaken three times, and every disbeliever and hypocrite will come out to him.”

Abd al-Aziz ibn Abdullah narrated to us; Ibrahim ibn Sad narrated to us, from his father, from his grandfather, from Abu Bakrah, from the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, who said: “The terror of the False Messiah will not enter Medina. On that day it will have seven gates, with two angels at each gate.”

Ali ibn Abdullah narrated to us; Muhammad ibn Bishr narrated to us; Misar narrated to us; Sad ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, from his father, from Abu Bakrah, from the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, who said: “The terror of the Messiah will not enter Medina. On that day it will have seven gates, with two angels at each gate.” Ibn Ishaq said: Salih ibn Ibrahim narrated from his father, who said: I came to Basra, and Abu Bakrah said to me: I heard the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, say this.

Abd al-Aziz ibn Abdullah narrated to us; Ibrahim narrated to us, from Salih, from Ibn Shihab, from Salim ibn Abdullah, that Abdullah ibn Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both, said: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, stood among the people, praised Allah as He deserves, then mentioned the Dajjal and said: “I warn you about him. There has been no prophet who did not warn his people about him. But I will tell you something about him that no prophet told his people: he is blind in one eye, while Allah is not blind in one eye.”

Yahya ibn Bukayr narrated to us; al-Layth narrated to us, from Uqayl, from Ibn Shihab, from Salim, from Abdullah ibn Umar, that the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: “While I was asleep, I was circumambulating the Kaaba. I saw a man with a brown complexion and straight hair, with water dripping—or pouring—from his head. I asked: ‘Who is this?’ They said: ‘The son of Mary.’ Then I turned and saw a large, ruddy man with curly hair and one blind eye, which looked like a floating grape. They said: ‘This is the Dajjal.’ The person who most resembles him is Ibn Qatan,” a man from Khuzaah.

Abd al-Aziz ibn Abdullah narrated to us; Ibrahim ibn Sad narrated to us, from Salih, from Ibn Shihab, from Urwah, that Aishah, may Allah be pleased with her, said: I heard the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, seek refuge during his prayer from the trial of the Dajjal.

Abdan narrated to us; my father informed me, from Shu'bah, from Abd al-Malik, from Rib'i, from Hudhayfah, from the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, who said about the Dajjal: “He will have water and fire with him. His fire will be cool water, and his water will be fire.” Abu Masud said: I heard this from the Messenger of Allah.

Sulayman ibn Harb narrated to us; Shu'bah narrated to us, from Qatadah, from Anas, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: “There has been no prophet who did not warn his community about the one-eyed liar. He is indeed one-eyed, while your Lord is not one-eyed. Written between his eyes is ‘disbeliever.’” Abu Hurairah and Ibn Abbas also reported it from the Prophet.

Abu al-Yaman informed us; Shuayb informed us, from al-Zuhri, who said: Ubaydullah ibn Abdullah ibn Utbah ibn Masud informed me that Abu Said said: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, told us a lengthy account about the Dajjal one day. Among what he told us was: “The Dajjal will come, but he will be forbidden to enter the mountain passes of Medina. He will stop in some of the salt flats near Medina. That day a man who is among the best of people will go out to him and say: ‘I testify that you are the Dajjal about whom the Messenger of Allah told us.’ The Dajjal will say: ‘What do you think? If I kill this man and then bring him back to life, will you still doubt my claim?’ They will say: ‘No.’ He will kill him and then bring him back to life. The man will say: ‘By Allah, I have never seen you more clearly for what you are than I do today.’ The Dajjal will then want to kill him, but he will not be allowed to do so.”

Abdullah ibn Maslamah narrated to us, from Malik, from Nuaim ibn Abdullah al-Mujmir, from Abu Hurairah, who said: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: “Angels stand at the mountain passes of Medina. Neither plague nor the Dajjal will enter it.”

Yahya ibn Musa narrated to me; Yazid ibn Harun narrated to us; Shu'bah informed us, from Qatadah, from Anas ibn Malik, from the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, who said: “The Dajjal will come to Medina and find angels guarding it, so he will not come near it”—he said—“nor will plague, if Allah wills.”

Abu al-Yaman informed us; Shuayb informed us, from al-Zuhri. Ismail narrated to us; my brother narrated to me, from Sulayman, from Muhammad ibn Abi Atiq, from Ibn Shihab, from Urwah ibn al-Zubayr, that Zaynab bint Abi Salamah told him, from Umm Habibah bint Abi Sufyan, from Zaynab bint Jahsh: One day the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, entered upon her in alarm, saying: “There is no god but Allah. Woe to the Arabs because of an evil that has drawn near. An opening this size has been made today in the barrier of Gog and Magog.” He made a circle with his thumb and the finger next to it. Zaynab bint Jahsh said: I asked: “Messenger of Allah, will we be destroyed while righteous people are among us?” He said: “Yes, when wickedness becomes widespread.”

Musa ibn Ismail narrated to us; Wuhayb narrated to us; Ibn Tawus narrated to us, from his father, from Abu Hurairah, from the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, who said: “The barrier of Gog and Magog will be opened by an amount like this.” Wuhayb formed a circle of ninety.

Abdan informed us; Abdullah informed us, from Yunus, from al-Zuhri, who said: Abu Salamah ibn Abd al-Rahman informed me that he heard Abu Hurairah, may Allah be pleased with him, say: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: “Whoever obeys me has obeyed Allah, and whoever disobeys me has disobeyed Allah. Whoever obeys my appointed leader has obeyed me, and whoever disobeys my appointed leader has disobeyed me.”

Ismail narrated to us: Malik narrated to me, from Abdullah ibn Dinar, from Abdullah ibn Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both, that the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: “Each of you is a shepherd, and each of you is responsible for his flock. The ruler over the people is a shepherd and is responsible for his flock. A man is a shepherd over his household and is responsible for his flock. A woman is a shepherd over her husband's household and his children and is responsible for them. A servant is a shepherd over his master's property and is responsible for it. Each of you is a shepherd, and each of you is responsible for his flock.”

Abu al-Yaman informed us; Shuayb informed us, from al-Zuhri, who said: Muhammad ibn Jubayr ibn Mutim used to relate that this report reached Muawiyah while he was with a delegation from Quraysh. Abdullah ibn Amr was saying that a king would arise from Qahtan. Muawiyah became angry, stood, praised Allah as He deserves, then said: “I have been told that some men among you relate reports that are neither in the Book of Allah nor transmitted from the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him. Those people are your ignorant ones. Beware of wishful notions that lead their followers astray. I heard the Messenger of Allah say: ‘This authority belongs to Quraysh. No one will oppose them while they uphold the religion without Allah casting him down on his face.’” Nuaim also reported it from Ibn al-Mubarak, from Mamar, from al-Zuhri, from Muhammad ibn Jubayr.

Ahmad ibn Yunus narrated to us; Asim ibn Muhammad narrated to us: I heard my father say that Ibn Umar said: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: “Authority will remain among Quraysh as long as two of them remain.”

Shihab ibn Abbad narrated to us; Ibrahim ibn Humayd narrated to us, from Ismail, from Qays, from Abdullah, who said: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: “There is no envy except in two cases: a man whom Allah has given wealth and enabled to spend it in the right cause, and a man whom Allah has given wisdom, by which he judges and which he teaches.”

Musaddad narrated to us; Yahya narrated to us, from Shu'bah, from Abu al-Tayyah, from Anas ibn Malik, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: “Listen and obey, even if an Ethiopian slave is appointed over you, whose head is like a raisin.”

Sulayman ibn Harb narrated to us; Hammad narrated to us, from al-Jad, from Abu Raja, from Ibn Abbas, who related that the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: “Whoever sees something from his ruler that he dislikes should be patient, for no one separates from the community by even a handspan and dies except that he dies a death of the pre-Islamic age.”
